articles.body:
No. 10 BYU (7-2, 4-2) vs. Baylor (6-3, 4-2)

Venue: LaVell Edwards Stadium (capacity: 62,073)

Radio: KSL 1160 AM/102.7 FM/BYU Radio Sirius XM 166

For BYU: The Cougars are coming off a painful rivalry loss at Utah, but their College Football Playoff hopes remain alive after only dropping one spot to No. 10 in the latest CFP poll.

If BYU wants any shot at playoff action, however, it needs to take care of business down the stretch, starting Saturday against an upstart, inspired Baylor squad. How the Cougars handle the Bears after last week's letdown will reveal a great deal about their CFP hopes.

BYU is scoring 31.0 points per game and allowing 19.8 points per contest, but has not won the turnover battle in more than a month.

For Baylor: All appeared lost for the Bears upon firing head coach Dave Aranda in October, but interim Joe Klanderman has managed to rally Baylor for two convincing wins since then to remain in the thick of the Big 12 title chase.

Baylor is scoring 31.9 points per game and allowing 17.0 points per game.

"We can't let the Utah loss linger into (this) week, but what we can do is use it as motivation to get better. We appreciate all the fans and everyone who supports us. We know we can play better, and it is my job to get these guys playing at a higher level." — BYU coach Kalani Sitake

"Our margin for error is razor-thin. You can't afford mental busts or lapses in effort against a top-10 team." — Baylor coach Joe Klanderman

articles.title: Why Haiti hosting the US in Miami feels like a homecoming
articles.summary: men’s national team in a Concacaf Nations League match in Miami, Haitian fans are already celebrating Les Grenadiers hosting its “home” game on their opponen...
articles.body:
A day before Haiti hosts the U.S. men's national team in a Concacaf Nations League match in Miami, Haitian fans are already celebrating Les Grenadiers hosting its "home" game on their opponent's soil. The match at Miami's Nu Stadium , a venue with tickets costing upwards of $158, is already nearly sold out as the Haitian community gets ready to cheer on the team.

On Friday evening, hundreds plan to gather at the Little Haiti Cultural Complex for a kickoff soirée featuring konpa group T-Vice and a rara band. Saturday morning, Haitian soccer legends promise to take the field at Oak Grove Park in North Miami, as a way to connect generations of Haitian soccer fans, celebrate the athletes and build excitement.

"Together, the events aim to create a home-like environment for Les Grenadiers, where music, food, national colors and soccer bring Haiti's presence into a stadium outside its borders," said Ernst "Zenno" Jean-Baptiste , a former national team player and coach, during a livestream promoting the events.

"We want them to feel that they are not arriving in an unfamiliar place," he said, referring to the players.

For local residents, community leaders and scholars, Saturday's matchup brings together two Haitian migration stories.

One is that of Haitians who have built communities across the U.S. while waiting for conditions in Haiti to improve. The other involves members of the Haitian diaspora, who represent their ancestral homeland and a "reverse-flow migration" as one scholar describes it.

The phenomenon has led to Haiti playing home games outside the country because incessant gang-fueled violence has locked them out.

"It's good news that Haiti is allowed to host its game in the Haitian-heavy Miami area," said Judite Blanc , a psychologist and associate professor at the University of Miami who is Haitian American.

"But still, hosting your match in the opposing team's territory creates an upside-down scenario."

Jean Berthol Bazile, a North Miami entrepreneur with Jean-Baptiste on the livestream, saw the unusual "home" game designation as a fitting arrangement for Haiti.

"This is the capital of the Haitian diaspora," said Bazile, who is reselling match tickets.

He added, "This is (poetic) justice for us, after being snubbed by FIFA not scheduling any of Haiti's World Cup matches in Miami."

Haiti has not played a senior men's national team match on its own soil since June 2021, when it hosted Canada in a World Cup qualifying match at Stade Sylvio Cator . The following month, Haiti's president was assassinated , leaving a governance vacuum that criminal organizations have exploited.

As gang violence escalated across Port-au-Prince, the stadium, located in the heart of the capital, became too dangerous to access. In March 2024, armed groups took control of the facility as a base of operations.

This week, on Nov. 11, newly deployed Salvadoran troops drove armed gangs from the stadium. The troops are now using the stadium as a military base.

Over the past five years, Haiti has played "home" games in Curaçao and Jamaica, whose facilities comply with FIFA and Concacaf's stadium guidelines for international matches. This fall, weeks after a post-game melee in the Dominican Republic, Concacaf allowed Haiti to play home matches in its opponents' territory.

The temporary movements reflect a feeling many Haitian immigrants waiting to go back home find familiar.

Edline Mompremier, another Miami resident, sums up the team's predicament.

"Haiti may be nomadic, but it is not homeless," said Mompremier, who plans to attend the match with her 9-year-old daughter.

Diaspora's heartbeat thrums ahead of match

In that sense, the team's experience mirrors that of Haitians in South Florida, home to one of the largest Haitian communities outside of Haiti.

According to a September 2026 report by the Migration Policy Institute ( MPI ), nearly 859,000 Haitian immigrants lived in the U.S. in 2024. Florida accounted for 48% of that population, while the Miami metropolitan area accounted for approximately 31% of Haitian immigrants nationwide.

From Homestead to Miami, Fort Lauderdale to Palm Beach, Haitians living in cities across the state are brimming with excitement. Grenadiers fever is also drawing Haitians far beyond South Florida, including many families who could not afford tickets to World Cup matches or to travel abroad.

For them, seeing the national team in person creates a connection that television broadcasts, streaming and long-distance travel cannot replicate. Although Haiti played a World Cup friendly in Miami earlier this year against Peru, this game holds more significance because Haiti is the host in a competitive match.

The timing also coincides with the Battle of Vertières, the Haitian Revolution combat associated with the team's namesake, on Nov. 18. The Haitian Football Federation and some event organizers have pushed the connection over social media in promoting the month's games.

"Everyone will wear their Haitian team jersey, bring flags, tchatchas and more to make noise," said Onèl Marius, who is traveling from Orlando with family to attend the game.

"We want the players to feel a homecoming atmosphere the minute they enter the stadium."

In the 1990s, the Haitian government launched a campaign called "Retounen Lakay" — Haitian Creole for "Return Home"— to encourage Haitians who had fled Duvalier's dictatorship to return to Haiti. Decades later, a similar campaign launched by Haiti's soccer Federation, "Return to the Stadium," has borne fruit for Haitian soccer.

Les Grenadiers, so named after Haitian Revolution soldiers, is made up entirely of diaspora players. Led by Spanish coach David Badia, all 25 players on this year's team were either born abroad or currently play for clubs mainly in Europe and North America.

Jeffrey Kassing , a professor at Arizona State University's School of Social and Behavioral Sciences, studies the relationship among soccer, migration and diaspora identity. He has seen this "reverse-flow migration" of players from wealthier countries representing their parents' countries of origin in various sports and locations. In a 2025 research article on the topic he co-authored, Kassing explains in detail how countries can draw on talent developed outside their borders to strengthen their national teams.

"In that sense, despite disadvantages to local-based players and some other sociocultural effects," Kassing said, "reverse-flow migration is a benefit to Haiti like it is to several countries — including Curaçao, Cape Verde, Morocco and Mexico, among others."

Blanc sees the phenomenon working in Haiti's diaspora-led team bringing it back to the FIFA World Cup after a 52-year absence. She said the reactions and solidarity that Haitians showed around the World Cup run prove that football has extraordinary power to unite and transform Haiti.

"Football is a powerful means for the country to bring unity and positive transformation," she said. "These players being raised in other systems can push the leaders to develop the sports infrastructure, youth development programs and other socio-economic projects."

Even with the benefits, Blanc said, Saturday's contrast is difficult to ignore. The Haitian players will still know they are not at home because Miami is not Port-au-Prince, she said. And numerically, she said, the U.S. team may still hold the advantage.

"It's good news that Haiti is allowed to host its game in the Haitian-heavy Miami area," Blanc said. "But still, hosting your match in the opposing team's territory creates an upside-down scenario."

As the opening whistle blows at 4:30 p.m. EST on Saturday, each team will try to take an upper hand in the tie before the return leg on Nov. 17 at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. Knocking out the USMNT to reach the tournament's semifinals will mean an automatic berth in the 2027 Gold Cup. In the two nations' last 10 meetings , LesGrenadiers recorded five defeats and five draws.

Still, fans like Rickenson Cher-Frère, the owner of a multi-service store in Fort Lauderdale that resells match tickets, believe Haiti can prevail. In yet another Facebook Live video from the Little Haiti Cultural Complex promoting pre-match events, Cher-Frère boasted about the impact of being in Miami.

"Haitians will not be subdued like smaller crowds," he said. "Our soul is here. We should beat the U.S."

This report is a collaboration between The Haitian Times and The Associated Press.

articles.title: Al Michaels Gets Choked Up During Tribute to Late Broadcaster Dan Hicks on “Thursday Night Football”
articles.summary: Hicks died unexpectedly of an “acute illness,” his wife Hannah Storm announced on Thursday, Nov. 12
articles.body:
Al Michaels got emotional in a tribute to Dan Hicks

Hicks, 64, died after an acute illness, his wife Hannah Storm announced on Thursday, Nov. 12

Hicks worked for NBC for 34 years, covering golf and Olympic events including swimming and alpine skiing

Al Michaels shared an emotional tribute to Dan Hicks during Thursday Night Football .

The broadcaster took a moment to honor the NBC sportscaster, whose death at the age of 64 was announced on Thursday, Nov. 12 by his wife Hannah Storm .

"All of us in the sports broadcasting business were shocked to learn this morning of the passing of Dan Hicks," Michaels, 82, said. "Dan joined NBC Sports in 1992, provided captions to so many iconic moments in golf, tennis and Notre Dame football, and he and Rowdy Gaines turned the calling of swimming at multiple Olympics into an art form."

Michaels continued, his voice breaking, "He was genial. He was compassionate. Great company. Had a world-class sense of humor. And on this very rough day for so many of us, we send our love to Hannah [Storm] and your three daughters. Wishing you strength and comfort."

Hicks died "following an acute illness," Storm shared in a social media post early on Thursday.

"He was a devoted husband of over 30 years, loving father to our three daughters, and cherished friend to so many," the ESPN broadcaster, 64, wrote. "His loss is immeasurable."

Storm continued: "Dan was truly one of a kind and, quite simply, the person everyone wanted to be around. When he walked into a room, he brought the energy, the laughter and the people together. He was endlessly kind, thoughtful and funny, and he made everyone feel like they mattered."

Hicks — who maintained a busy work schedule yet made time to root on one of his daughters in the Chicago Marathon last month before his unexpected death — was set to call this weekend's Notre Dame game, something he had done for seven seasons.

Jason Benetti, NBC's Sunday Night Baseball play-by-play voice, will step in alongside analyst Jason Garrett for the game against Boston College on Saturday, Nov. 14.

Among the many who shared tributes to Hicks on Thursday was swimmer Michael Phelps .

The late broadcaster called all 28 of Phelps' Olympic medal-winning races from 2004 through 2016, according to NBC Sports .

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!

"This one hurts," Phelps, 41, wrote on Instagram . "Really don't even know what to say right now. There are certain voices in sports that you hear and instantly know who it is…. Dan had one of those voices. A voice that so many of us grew up listening to, a voice that brought some of the biggest moments in sports to life…. And for me, a voice that will forever be part of my story. But he was so much more than that to me. He was a friend."

Phelps added, "Dan, thank you for the friendship, the memories, and everything you did for me and our sport. Gonna miss you, my friend."

articles.title: Tennessee RB injured and cited for reckless driving, will miss Texas A&M game
articles.summary: Tennessee running back Daune Morris will be out for the Texas A&M game, after he was cited for reckless driving and injured in a car crash.
articles.body:
Tennessee will be without one of its star running backs against Texas A&M at Kyle Field on Saturday after he was cited for reckless driving and injured following a car crash.

According to a police report, running back Daune Morris sustained non-life-threatening injuries, including a broken leg, during a car accident Friday morning. He will at least miss the game against the Aggies, which is the first matchup between the two programs in College Station since 2016.

The sophomore from Chattanooga has recorded 434 rushing yards and three touchdowns this season. Morris is the team's second-leading rusher, behind DeSean Bishop, and leads Tennessee's No. 1 rushing attack in the SEC.

In last week's 34-6 win over No. 6 Kentucky, Morris rushed for 85 yards on five carries and one touchdown. He has averaged 6.58 yards per carry and hauled in six receptions for 35 yards so far this season. The Vols will greatly miss Morris' physicality and speed, which rank No. 11 nationally in yards per game.

That's one of Texas A&M's major mismatches against Tennessee this weekend. The Aggies rank No. 11 in rush defense, allowing 129.89 rushing yards per contest. However, Morris being out is a massive hit to the depth of the Vols' running back room entering Saturday's showdown at Kyle Field .

Tennessee boasts a 7-2 record and is ranked No. 8 in the College Football Playoff rankings, allowing an opportunity for Texas A&M to play spoiler in Week 11.

articles.title: Cara y cruz para Lookman
articles.standfirst: El extremo del Atlético de Madrid se reivindicó con Nigeria registrando una asistencia... pero salió lesionado antes del descanso
articles.summary: El extremo del Atlético de Madrid se reivindicó con Nigeria registrando una asistencia... pero salió lesionado antes del descanso
articles.body: Ademola Lookman necesitaba utilizar este parón de selecciones con Nigeria para intentar reivindicarse. Suya fue la asistencia del primer gol contra Tanzania (3-1). Antes del descanso, sin embargo, tuvo que pedir el cambio. Titular en una doble punta junto al exsevillista Akor Adams, ahora en las filas del Venecia, el atacante del Atlético de Madrid apenas tardó dos minutos en servirle el pase de gol del 1-0 a Alhassan Yusuf. Nigeria recuperó alto tras pérdida, recibió el balón dentro del área y filtro un buen servicio para la llegada del extremo de New England Revolution desde atrás. A partir de ahí, la realidad es que Lookman tampoco se mostró excesivamente participativo: apenas tocó 12 balones, no completó el único regate que intentó e incurrió en cinco pérdidas. Ya en el tiempo de descuento de la primera parte, sintió unas molestias que le obligaron a abandonar el campo. Su lugar lo ocupó Moses Simon. A la vuelta de vestuarios, además, Eric Chelle dio entrada a Ndidi y un Tolu Arokodare que, en cuestión de 15', dejó el partido resuelto con un doblete. El delantero del Ajax atraviesa un momento de forma increíble. Entre club y selección, ya suma 15 goles este curso. Nigeria, con esta victoria, se asienta en la segunda plaza de su grupo de clasificación para la Copa África 2027 que le daría acceso al torneo. El objetivo, en cualquier caso, pasa por arrebatarle la primera posición a Guinea-Bisáu, que les goleó en el partido de ida disputado en el parón de septiembre-octubre. El próximo martes se vuelven a medir a Tanzania. Pero, salvo sorpresa, no estará Lookman.

articles.title: Southampton Spygate: EFL warn clubs over social media posts
articles.summary: The English Football League (EFL) warns its members about their usage of posts on social media.
articles.body:
The English Football League (EFL) has warned its members about their usage of posts on social media that might target other sides regarding disciplinary issues.

In September, Wrexham aimed a Spygate -based dig at Southampton in a video that featured their owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney in a cheeky social media post.

This came before the Dragons played Saints, eventually winning the Championship game 2-1 at the Racecourse Ground.

Wrexham's owners appeared on Wrexham's X account, which started with Reynolds emerging from behind a tree.

In a skit nominally aimed at promoting shirt sponsor Firefox, the Deadpool star said: "Today, for no particular reason, we want to talk about the importance of privacy."

A few weeks later, Southampton fired back at Wrexham after the Welsh club had been fined by the EFL for fielding two ineligible players.

Saints commented "hope you've double checked this one lads" on their X account under Wrexham's team news post for a following game against Sheffield United.

Birmingham City also joined in with the Spygate themed posts, with a graphic of both clubs' badges cut into grass hedges, shown through the eye of binoculars before playing each other in September.

The EFL has since sent a letter to club chairs and executives, advising clubs to avoid posts that could have a reputational impact.

articles.title: Ronaldinho: Brazil legend set for first start for Italian club Ravenna aged 46
articles.summary: Brazil great Ronaldinho is set to make his first competitive start in more than a decade when Ravenna face local rivals Forli in Italy's third division on Sunday.
articles.body:
Brazil great Ronaldinho is set to make his first competitive start in more than a decade when Ravenna face local rivals Forli in Italy's third division on Sunday.

The former Barcelona and AC Milan playmaker, 46, is in line to make his first appearance for Ravenna since joining the Serie C club in August .

His last competitive appearance came for Brazilian side Fluminense in September 2015 .

Ravenna manager Andrea Mandorlini said on Friday that Ronaldinho would start the match as one of his side's three forwards.

"He will play from the start, there's no doubt," Mandorlini told reporters. "Then together we will decide how long he plays.

"He is one of the greatest players of the modern era. And we have to get a result. We always play with three forwards. He will be one of the three."

Former Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldinho initially joined the Italian club as an investor in August, but said he had ambitions of scoring one final goal to take his career tally to 300.

"His objective is romantic, to try to score his last goal," club owner Ignazio Cipriani said earlier this year.

"His involvement is not a token gesture or a marketing stunt to get people talking about us."

The Brazilian arrived in Italy on Friday and will have only one training session with his team-mates before Sunday's match.

A temporary stand has been created at Ravenna's Stadio Bruno Benelli to accommodate the expected crowd, with supporters hoping to catch a glimpse of the World Cup winner in action for potentially the final time.

Ravenna forward Simone Rabbi has also said that Ronaldinho will take any penalties awarded to Ravenna, who are second in the table after 13 matches.

articles.title: Bob Chesney, UCLA Reportedly Nearing Contract Extension amid Undefeated Start to Season
articles.summary: UCLA Bruins coach Bob Chesney is close to agreeing to terms on a contract extension that would keep him in Westwood, according to The Athletic's Ira Gorawara and Bruce Feldman.
articles.body:
UCLA Bruins coach Bob Chesney is close to agreeing to terms on a contract extension that would keep him in Westwood, according to The Athletic's Ira Gorawara and Bruce Feldman .

The Bruins won just three games last season, but Chesney has led them to an undefeated 9-0 record this season with three games remaining. UCLA was ranked No. 4 in the College Football Playoff committee's most recent rankings, the highest position in the program's history.

UCLA lost starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava to a season-ending knee injury against Oregon in early October, but the team has leaned on its strong defense and a rushing attack led by running back Wayne Knight, who followed Chesney from James Madison.

Chesney has won at every level of collegiate football. He has won eight conference championships in his 16 seasons as a head coach, per UCLA . Chesney won a conference championship with Division III Salve Regina, two conference titles at Division II Assumption and four conference championships at Holy Cross.

In 2025, Chesney led the James Madison Dukes to their first Sun Belt championship and College Football Playoff appearance.

UCLA fired former coach Deshaun Foster after the Bruins lost their first three games of the 2025 season. Foster finished his stint at UCLA with a 5-10 record. The Bruins won three of their first four games under interim coach Tim Skipper, but they ultimately closed out the season with five consecutive losses.

The Bruins are heading into Friday's matchup against Illinois as the only undefeated team in the Big Ten or SEC.

articles.title: Nations League: Wales out to derail Norway's repair job in Oslo
articles.summary: Norway's golden generation host Wales in a crunch Nations League clash on Saturday, aiming to end a rare losing streak for Erling Haaland and company.
articles.body:
As the first snow of the season falls in Oslo, the clean-up operation at Norway's home stadium is in full swing – tractors on the pitch, Norwegian Football Federation staff getting stuck in with their shovels.

This has been a problematic pitch in the past, with even the great Erling Haaland questioning its condition , external back in March, before it was fixed during the summer.

By their recent, historic high standards, Norway need something of a repair job themselves.

Having gone through 2025 unbeaten and then soared to the quarter-finals of the World Cup, Norway have lost three games in a row for the first time in a decade.

Granted, two of those were against Portugal, whereas their losing run in 2016 included defeats in Azerbaijan and Belarus.

But this is Norway's golden generation. With Haaland, Martin Odegaard and a glut of other elite talents at their disposal, expectations are greater than ever.

Thumping Italy twice on their way to World Cup qualification was one thing – their first major tournament since 1998 – but beating Brazil in their last-16 tie in New Jersey underlined their credentials as an emerging force in international football.

So, when this Nations League campaign came around, Stale Solbakken's men were expected to be jostling with Portugal for top spot.

Instead, they find themselves at the bottom of Group A4 with just one win from four games, level with third-placed Wales on three points but below them because of their head-to-head record.

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC Two Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru and 5 Live Sports Extra, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

How do you stop Haaland? Wales show how it's done

Odegaard backing Norway to avenge Wales defeat

Wales' only victory of the campaign so far was against Norway in Cardiff a month ago, and on Saturday they are bidding to join Portugal and world champions Spain as the only teams to win competitive matches in Oslo over the past three years.

"The way we look at it is this is the type of game we want to be playing in," Wales head coach Craig Bellamy tells BBC Sport Wales.

"I see a collective team that you have to like but, individually, very much so as well. So that's a good challenge.

"We've all been aware of their threat. The World Cup proved that. And I just don't see them going anywhere for the next five, 10 years either."

There is much on the line for Wales and Norway in Oslo.

While either team could still reach the Nations League quarter-finals, the priority is to avoid relegation from the top tier.

Finishing third or higher would also guarantee top seeding for Euro 2028 qualifying, enabling them to avoid being drawn alongside the continent's heavyweights.

"It'll go a long way to us having an opportunity of being seeded one, which is huge for us, but it isn't going to be given to us," Bellamy adds.

"We have to go out there tomorrow and try and take it. So, for me, it's fight fire with fire. I'm expecting them to really come with big intensity and it's up to us to match it.

Norway's echoes of Wales' golden generation

If Norway are at the peak of their golden era, Wales are still basking in the afterglow of theirs.

They had been absent from major tournaments for 58 years before a team featuring Gareth Bale and Aaron Ramsey took them to the semi-finals of Euro 2016.

Like Norway's exploits this summer, that tournament in France changed the landscape of Welsh football, paving the way for future qualifications at Euro 2020 and the 2022 World Cup.

"I think that we are both small countries, so I can agree on that," Norway head coach Solbakken says of the comparison.

"Everyone will remember that summer of 2026 in Norway, as Wales did 10 years ago."

If you want to stretch the analogy to tenuous lengths, you could also note that the two teams were built around the heroics of hitherto ponytailed forwards (Bale and Haaland) and the creativity of Arsenal playmakers (Ramsey and Odegaard).

Few remain of that Welsh vintage by now, though captain Ben Davies is one.

"They've got players now performing at the highest level in world football and starring in that as well," the Tottenham Hotspur defender says.

"Great for Norwegian football, a challenge for us, but one we're looking forward to."

Davies played an important role in Wales' win over Norway last month, at the heart of a defence which managed to contain Haaland.

The 33-year-old has also been part of a Spurs backline which denied the Norwegian a goal in a 4-0 win at Manchester City two years ago.

Not that Davies is going to mention that in Oslo.

"He's a world-class player," he says. "Maybe he had an off-night [in Cardiff] but we worked hard, stuck to our job and we defended really well. Hopefully we'll do that again."

articles.title: El Barça sufre por el central
articles.standfirst: La situación económica complica a la Dirección Deportiva ejecutar las principales opciones
articles.summary: La situación económica complica a la Dirección Deportiva ejecutar las principales opciones
articles.body: Hansi Flick y Deco tienen claro que les gustaría reforzar la defensa en el mercado de enero. La zaga es la línea que se está viendo más mermada a causa de las lesiones y el Director Deportivo y el preparador desean apuntalarla. Pero la intención es hacerlo con un futbolista de calidad y que tenga recorrido en la entidad: no quieren firmar a un profesional para sólo seis meses. Y el perfil requerido implica una inversión que, en estos momentos, no pueden concretar, de ahí las dificultades y que se sucedan las semanas sin que haya avances destacados al respecto. El Barça se mantiene en la regla 1:1 gracias, entre otros motivos, a la renovación de Raphinha, ya que con su nuevo vínculo se prolonga y reduce su amortización y, además, el aumento de su ficha no se hará momento efectiva porque se ejecutará el próximo curso, por lo que no afecta a la masa salarial actual. Pero la ampliación de Xavi Espart, la más que inminente de Marc Bernal y las de Brian Fariñas y Gerard Martín, que están en marcha, sí que repercuten en el montante total de lo que cuesta el vestuario, y de ahí algunos de los problemas del Barcelona para fichar en enero. Tanto en los despachos del Spotify Camp Nou como en los de la Ciudad Deportiva tienen claro que no desean incorporar a algún futbolista para sólo unos meses o que no eleve la calidad del vestuario actual. El objetivo es apuntalar la zaga con un central importante, y esa contratación conlleva un desembolso que ahora no pueden acometer, salvo que haya una salida y, de momento, no hay ninguna operación avanzada en ese sentido. Todas las miradas están puestas en Alejandro Balde. La entidad confía en que el lateral izquierdo se vaya en enero, pero, a día de hoy, su futuro es una incógnita. Hasta ahora se ha mostrado reticente a abandonar la disciplina culé y las opciones que ha tenido sobre la mesa no le han acabado de satisfacer, pero su ostracismo, confían en el club, puede provocar un cambio en su parecer en las próximas semanas. En los despachos no lo tienen, no obstante, claro... De todas formas, las puertas del Barça están abiertas también para otros futbolistas de la plantilla de Hansi Flick. Necesita vender. No todo el equipo está en venta, hay profesionales intocables (Raphinha, Pedri, Cubarsí, Lamine...), pero los ejecutivos están dispuestos a escuchar propuestas por muchos jugadores. Deco y su equipo de colaboradores manejan una lista de centrales futuribles, pero todos se escapan de sus márgenes económicos actuales. Aunque, a día de hoy, los profesionales del área deportiva no descartan nada. De hecho, existe la esperanza de que habrá algún refuerzo en la próxima ventana de incorporaciones, aunque no les está resultando fácil. Ya sabían desde verano que si necesitaban firmar alguna alta en enero sería complicado como consecuencia del estado de las finanzas. Pero su trabajo no cesa y están manteniendo contactos y reuniones con varios profesionales, algunos cuya identidad no ha trascendido aún, que se ajustan al perfil ansiado. A pesar de sus deseos, nombres como los de Tah, Bastoni, Nijstad, Gvardiol, Natan, Reis... no son opciones factibles en estos momentos ya que no están a su alcance económico. Pero en el Barça no descartan nada porque la situación puede cambiar: puede haber una baja inesperada, un candidato puede forzar su salida aunque sea en la modalidad de cesión... Cruzan los dedos.

articles.title: Scotland 2-1 North Macedonia: John McGinn scores double as hosts toil in Nations League encounter
articles.summary: Match report as John McGinn scores twice in Scotland's win over North Macedonia at Hampden; Aston Villa midfielder gives hosts lead after McTominay and Gilmour go close; Rastoder's header levels scoring; McGinn penalty seals win after Gannon-Doak fouled; Scotland face Switzerland next
articles.body:
The hosts were booed off at half-time with the game goalless but there was a sense of relief - rather than joy - at the final whistle after McGinn's penalty secured the three points after Elmin Rastoder's header cancelled out the Aston Villa midfielder's opener.

The win means Scotland can still finish second in Group B1 after Slovenia were held by Switzerland, but will have to win in St Gallen on Monday and hope North Macedonia do them a favour in their final game.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli secured his first win at Hampden on a night when skipper Andy Robertson earned his 102nd cap to equal the appearance record held by Sir Kenny Dalglish.

The returning Scott McTominay nearly grabbed an opener after 16 minutes but he was denied by Stole Dimitrievski in the North Macedonia goal after turning and shooting sharply. The keeper then denied Che Adams and McTominay again before the Napoli midfielder attempted to recreate his famous Denmark overhead kick to no avail.

Boos rang around Hampden as the players trudged off at the interval and Billy Gilmour did little to lift the collective mood straight after the break when he fired over with the goal gaping following good work by Adams.

Scotland did take the lead soon after, however, Adams outmuscling his North Macedonian counterpart to set the onrushing McGinn away into the box before he curled his effort into the net.

Rastoder stunned Hampden less than three minutes later, leaping highest to glance his header past Angus Gunn from a corner, but Dimitrievski went from hero to villain with a little over 15 minutes remaining, bringing down Ben Gannon-Doak when the winger seemed to be running the ball out of play.

A VAR review followed, allowing McGinn to step up and deliver a first win in Glasgow for Pocognoli, but it is a performance that will raise more questions than answers.

16: BIG SAVE! Scott McTominay controls the ball with his back to the goal, then turns sharply and shoots but Stole Dimitrievski gets down well to his left and keeps it out.

22: OVER! Andy Robertson delivers a free-kick into the box but Kieran Tierney's header loops over the bar.

27: SAVE! John McGinn's corner is met by Che Adams at the front post before his header takes a big deflection. It looks like it's heading in but Dimitrievski is equal to it again.

35: OVER! McTominay tries an acrobatic effort with an overhead kick but it sails over the bar and out of play.

39: MCTOMINAY DENIED! The ball is threaded into the feet of McTominay and he shoots from a tight angle but the goalkeeper makes another save to keep it level!

46: HOW HAS HE MISSED?! Adams capitalises on a loose back pass and squares the ball to Billy Gilmour. All he has to do is guide it on target and it is a goal but he skies it over the bar!

54: GOAL! Adams outmuscles the defender before poking the ball forward allowing McGinn to race onto it before curling the opener into the back of the net.

57: GOAL! North Macedonia shock Scotland with a quickfire equaliser. The corner is whipped into the box and Rastoder is there to glance it into the bottom corner.

75: GOAL! McGinn scores from the spot to restore Scotland's lead

Pocognoli 'satisfied' with first home win

Scotland head coach Sebastian Pocognoli:

"I'm happy to get the first win at home. It's important and we knew before the game that it will help to build a winning culture.

"In terms of what we produced on the pitch, I know exactly what we worked on this week. I'm quite satisfied about what I saw in some moments of the game, the work on the ball and off the ball.

"It was not always perfect, but I know that what we worked on in the last two days happened many times on the pitch. And for me that's very important. On top of that, we created a lot of chances that we should score.

"Off the ball, I think we were quite aggressive. We recovered a number of balls that we managed well in some moments of transition. We created a big chance for Billy (Gilmour) from this also. So that's a new approach of the game. Not everything was perfect, but there was a lot to take to move forward.

"After the first goal, I think we need to learn to not drop the intensity. Because after the first goal, for five minutes, I really feel like we dropped the intensity and the focus. And we conceded a goal from a set-piece. And I had the same feeling after the second goal. So, it's something that we need to fix."

Robertson: We have to be patient with new style

Scotland captain Andy Robertson speaking to BBC Sport:

"I thought we showed glimpses of good stuff. We tried to be patient on the ball, tried to keep the ball, I think we did that well at times, but also at times it broke down because the quality wasn't there at times so we're still trying to piece it all together.

"It's a different way of playing and that's what we are working on in the training ground. It wasn't always perfect, but no international game is easy and we're all delighted in the changing room to get that win and hopefully other people have a smile on their face too.

"Every formation can be played differently, there are so many different variations of this formation. We're trying to implement what the manager and coaches want us to do on the training ground and we're working really hard.

"Yes, it's not going to be perfect right away but everything is working towards us going into the qualifiers for the Euros. We're still trying to learn it and we believe in what the manager is trying to teach us to do and we have to be patient with that.

"I know people don't see us train and see the work we're doing in the background, so I can get why people are frustrated but there is an idea behind what we are doing and like you say at times we lacked that quality.

"Obviously the Slovenia at home game made it unrealistic, or tougher [to qualify]. We'll go over to Monday and we'll give everything we can to win that game. We're in a position where we have to rely on other results."

On equaling Dalglish's appearance record: "It feels amazing for me and my family, it's an amazing achievement. I've been around here for a long time. I've had highs, I've had lows, I've sometimes had praise and had criticism."

John McGinn to Sky Sports on Andy Robertson's record-equalling night:

"Amazing - he deserves everything that is coming his way. The biggest credit I can give him is that he is always available, always willing to help his country. Whether he is at 60, 70, 80 per cent, or 100.

"I'm sure Monday will be a special occasion for him but he'll give the boring answer that it will only be special if we get three points."

Analysis: McGinn takes centre stage on record-equalling night for Robertson

It will be a night that Andy Robertson never forgets but a game most Scotland fans will blank from their collective memories fairly quickly.

The skipper equalled Sir Kenny Dalglish's record of 102 caps but it was fellow Scotland stalwart John McGinn who spared the home side's blushes on a drab evening in Glasgow.

Scotland looked slow in their build-up, even if there were first-half chances, but when the goal finally did come the floodgates did not open. Instead, North Macedonia, who hadn't scored since November 18, 2025, equalised and could have gone in front.

The natives were understandably restless but were ultimately relieved when Stole Dimitrievski clumsily brought down Gannon-Doak, allowing McGinn to be the hero again.

The Aston Villa captain was quick to remind everyone that a new style takes time to bed in and that is true. Scotland are moving away from the comforts and success of the Steve Clarke era, but questions will be asked of Pocognoli's insistence on using wing-backs and one upfront at home with a comfortable win expected.

Scotland have something to play for when they travel to Switzerland for their final Group B1 game, with promotion still up for grabs. Robertson should play on Monday to become Scotland's most-capped player outright. How sweet it would be if his 103rd appearance for his country was a winning one.

Scotland's remaining Nations League Group B1 fixtures

articles.title: England 0-1 Portugal: Max Dowman makes debut off the bench as U21s suffer defeat in friendly
articles.summary: Match report as England U21s lost to Portugal in a friendly; Afonso Moreira's first-half strike secured the win for Portugal; Max Dowman made his debut off the bench but could not stop Lee Carsley's side suffering back-to-back defeats
articles.body:
Dowman, aged 16, 10 months and 13 days, stepped off the bench with around half an hour remaining to make his debut, but Moreira's first half strike secured the victory for Portugal on the evening.

Lee Carsley's side have now suffered successive defeats for the first time since March 2021 following their loss to the Republic of Ireland in their last European Championship qualifying match in October.

England's preparations for next year's tournament did not get off to an ideal start as Bayer Leverkusen forward Moreira put the visitors ahead at the break.

Portugal's superiority continued in the second half and the hosts had to rely on a string of Tommy Setford saves to keep them in the contest, but the Arsenal goalkeeper could not stop them from falling to defeat.

Neither side did anything by the way of hurting their opponents through the opening quarter of an hour, with England's only real sight of goal came when Divin Mubama tried to catch Joao Carvalho off his line from range but fired wide.

Portugal forced Setford into action with their first shot on target of the contest when Mezian Mesloub cut inside and fired a low effort.

The visitors were beginning to get on top and they had their opener in the 38th minute when Moreira fired low at goal with a shot which squeezed under Setford and crept over the line.

England were nowhere near their best and Portugal threatened once more just before half-time when Mesloub slammed into the side netting from close range.

Setford was becoming busier as the game went on and he adjusted his body magnificently to tip Gustavo Sa's deflected effort wide.

England finally warmed into the match in the 75th minute when Mikey Moore's shot straight at Carvalho.

The hosts enjoyed their best spell of pressure in the final 10 minutes as they looked for an equaliser, but were unable to find a way through despite efforts from Divine Mukasa, Moore and Stephen Mfuni.

articles.title: Jesus Owono: Goalkeeper gets 12-game suspension for tackle which resulted in death of Jesus de Miguel
articles.summary: Jesus Owono is given a 12-match suspension by the Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee after his challenge which resulted in the death of Jesus de Miguel.
articles.body:
FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been given a 12-match suspension by the Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee after his challenge which resulted in the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

Owono, 25, was sent off after colliding with De Miguel during the closing stages of the second-tier match between their two respective sides on 2 November.

De Miguel died the following day, aged 30.

The disciplinary committee said it had to base its decision "on the facts expressly recorded in the referee's report", which stated the player "was sent off for 'violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play'.

"The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge."

The committee added the "nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances" means that "the maximum sanction, a 12-match suspension, is justified".

Separately, the federation has decided the game between the two sides, which was abandoned seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred, will not be replayed.

"This avoids having to resume play from the precise moment at which the tragic incident occurred," it said.

The teams were drawing 2-2 at the time and that result will now stand, with a federation committee saying that was the "most respectful course of action, given the extraordinary and tragic circumstances of this case".

Owono's club issued a statement on the goalkeeper's behalf on 4 November, in which he said he was experiencing "the most difficult days" of his life and felt "enormous pain" about De Miguel's death.

On Thursday, FC Andorra manager Carles Manso said Equatorial Guinea international Owono is yet to decide whether he will return to football following the incident.

Manso said Owono is currently spending time with his family and is "completely free to make any decision" with regard to a potential return, adding: "What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him.

"We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

"When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that [he will do so]."

articles.body: El Real Madrid Castilla conquistó el Nou Estadi con una victoria por la mínima ante el Nàstic (0-1). El filial blanco firmó un encuentro serio, llevó la iniciativa durante buena parte del choque y encontró en Pol Fortuny al autor del único tanto de la tarde. La expulsión de Nico Van Rijn en el minuto 58 facilitó la gestión de una ventaja que los visitantes ya no dejaron escapar. El Castilla salió decidido a mandar y encontró el gol en el minuto 10. Fortuny conectó un buen disparo que Ayesa tocó, pero no pudo evitar que acabara dentro de la portería. Los visitantes mantuvieron su propuesta y el propio Fortuny estuvo cerca de firmar el segundo tanto en el 55’, cuando su lanzamiento se estrelló en el poste. Tres minutos después, el encuentro tomó otro rumbo. Tras una revisión arbitral, Van Rijn vio la segunda tarjeta amarilla y dejó al Nàstic en inferioridad numérica. Con un jugador más, el Castilla pudo administrar su ventaja ante un rival que mejoró con diez hombres intentó reaccionar en los últimos minutos, especialmente a través de Darío Ramírez. Sin embargo, el conjunto madrileño resistió el empuje final. articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino: What can Manchester United fans expect from new boss?
articles.summary: What can Manchester United fans expect from their new manager Mauricio Pochettino?  BBC Sport gets an insight from Toby Alderweireld, who played under him at Spurs.
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino heads to Old Trafford with a reputation for "brutal" pre-seasons, an obsession with fitness and a no-nonsense approach.

Manchester United confirmed on Friday that Pochettino will become their manager on 18 November - replacing Michael Carrick - and has signed a contract until June 2029.

So what should the players and staff expect when the Argentine takes control at the end of next week?

BBC Sport spoke to Toby Alderweireld, who spent four years playing for Pochettino at Tottenham during a successful period where they reached the Champions League final and finished second in the Premier League.

How Ferguson-inspired Pochettino can succeed where Carrick failed at Man Utd

Pochettino a decade in Man Utd's making - but Carrick deserves better

Alderweireld, 37, says Pochettino has a no-nonsense approach to management and that he can get the best out of a squad, as long as you do it his way.

"He is very approachable but you need to follow his plan. If you don't follow his plan, you go on the side and you're not coming back any more.

"You need to think about team, team, team. If you're thinking about yourself, you're gone.

"As a player you have your own life, your own situation but he says 'look, I understand and you can talk to me about it but the team is number one' - that's the way it is and if you're not following it, he'll put you on the sideline.

"He's straightforward, has his own ideas and maybe you agree with them or don't, that's up to you. But you need to follow him and I think that's something Manchester United need - a big character, everyone in the same direction, following the plan and if not, no problem, you can go. He's the main man.

"He's a very smart man, knows how to talk to the press and what to say. He will create an environment like 'it's us against the world' - we are getting fit, we are together as a team. It doesn't matter what people say, let's work together and get results together.

"At Spurs there was coaching staff but he will be there. He knows everything. If he's not there, he's looking at video and data. He knows everything about the players on and off the pitch - the players will be watched.

"He is, in a positive way, a control freak because he says your body is your weapon and it needs to be ready to perform."

Manchester United have been criticised this season for an apparent lack of fitness and for not running enough in games - they rank in the bottom five in the league for distance covered and most high-intensity runs.

Alderweireld says Pochettino's number one demand is fitness and running .

"First of all he made us very fit. Pre-season was brutal.

"The way he wants to play - on the front foot, putting people under pressure, a high line, very dynamic play - you need to run. You need to be capable of running and be capable of high intensity runs - the basic is to be fit.

"Every manager wants a good pre-season and time to give the players their ideas and the fitness. But the players are going to feel straight away that it's a different level.

"This is every day at the training ground, it's 100% - that's what he asks, what he demands. It will be a big difference for the players and they're going to see results there straight away.

"In the Champions League semi-final, we were 3-0 down [against Ajax] and he didn't have a tactical half-time talk. He just said 'you're going to be physical, you're going to fight, you only need one goal to be back in the game, believe that everything is possible'.

"That was a big moment because we were nowhere near Ajax at that time, especially in that game. But we changed everything by intensity, by duels. I remember the long ball to [Fernando] Llorente and just fighting and asking 'how badly do you want it?' It changed from that moment."

articles.title: Duncan Ferguson: Glentoran boss 'made up' with first win as manager on home debut
articles.summary: Glentoran manager Duncan Ferguson said he is "made up" with his first three points on his home debut, after a 2-1 win over Bangor.
articles.body:
At the third time of asking, Duncan Ferguson is finally up and running as Glentoran manager.

After two draws to start his tenure in the Irish Premiership, a home debut for the former Everton striker had late drama under the Friday night lights at the Oval.

Jordan Stewart, dubbed the "wee man" by big Dunc after his first game, celebrated his contract extension by scoring the opening goal and, in a largely uneventful game, it looked like that would be the difference.

However, that all changed when Ben Cushnie equalised for Bangor in the 83rd minute, but there was more drama to follow as Cal Weatherup raced onto a long ball to slot home the winner with three minutes remaining and secure a first win for Ferguson as boss.

"I'm delighted to get my first three points at home, I'm absolutely made up," Ferguson said after the game.

"The boys kept on going until the very end."

Weatherup's late goal gives Ferguson first Glens win

Ferguson's first game in the Irish League was meant to be at home to Ballymena United on 24 October, but Storm Boelo and a waterlogged pitch delayed his highly-anticipated debut in the league.

Stewart scored the equaliser at then-leaders Coleraine in his first outing in the dugout the following week, and the Glens were then held to a goalless draw at Carrick Rangers.

But on Friday, Ferguson finally announced himself to the home support in east Belfast.

Despite a controlled first half and Stewart's opener, Ferguson felt that his side "sat too deep" before Bangor's equaliser, which came through former Glentoran man Cushnie.

But it was teenager Weatherup who was ultimately the difference, with a finish that Ferguson would have been proud of in his playing days as he slotted the ball between the legs of the onrushing Patrick Solis Grogan for his first goal of the campaign.

Ferguson said he was "made up" for the 18-year-old, who replaced Pat Hoban midway through the second half.

"We showed good character. We showed a bit of resilience," added the 54-year-old.

"They put us under pressure in the second half but that will happen. You're not going to dominate a game for the whole game at any level.

"I was delighted the boys showed character and resilience to get back into the game."

Given their mixed start to the season, a charge at the Irish Premiership title is going to be a long shot.

But if the Glens are to have any aspirations of a first Gibson Cup since 2009 then it is important for them to keep pace with those above.

Leaders Linfield and nearest challengers Coleraine both were comfortable winners on Friday, while Larne bounced back from their poor recent win to beat Dungannon Swifts.

Glentoran are 14 points off the Blues but have a game in hand, and they face another tricky home test against Cliftonville next Friday to try and build upon the win over the Seasiders.

As he reflected on his start to the league, Ferguson admitted "I think we need to get better overall.

"We're not conceding many goals, but we just have to create more.

"That's the hardest part of the game, but we look solid and that's the main thing.

"I'm happy with the group and the league is very close together, from top to bottom".

With that in mind, especially as he continues his early steps in the league, it's just "one game at a time" for Ferguson, rather than thinking too far ahead.

"We've just got to keep going. I think that is seven or eight games undefeated now," he added.

"We have to keep going and keep winning. We're a big club and the fans want us to keep winning, and I'm glad we got the three points for them today."
